evidence: Ran the shipped binary in an rsync copy outside the repository: `tp review <spec>` on spec/1.41.0.md, spec/0.36.0.md and spec/1.44.0.md, then counted under four segmentation rules. On 1.41.0's architect prompt: terminator-only split 60 sentences / 7 prohibitions (11.7%); non-empty lines 49 / 6 (12.2%); line-then-terminator 85 / 7 (8.2%); terminator-ending only 60 / 6 (10.0%). Across the four roles of that spec, line-then-terminator gives 85-86 sentences and 7-9 prohibitions (8.1-10.6%). No rule returns 57, and none returns 14%. The quoted line is verbatim in internal/cli/review.go:812 (with double quotes, not single).
note: Two separate problems. (1) The pair is not reproducible: my range is 6-9 prohibitions in 47-103 sentences, 8.1-12.2%, never 8 of 57 and never 14%. (2) The denominator is not a property of 'the review prompt' at all — the emitted prompt embeds a spec-derived checklist, so the same rule gives 60 sentences for spec/1.41.0.md, 60 for spec/1.44.0.md and 103 for spec/0.36.0.md. A single figure cannot describe it. The conclusion — that a real minority of the emission steers by ban, of order one sentence in ten — survives every rule I tried, and §4a's decision does not depend on the figure. This is the class CLAUDE.md names as 'a figure whose counting rule was never stated'; spec/candidates.md:304 repeats the same 14% figure, so the unstated rule has already propagated to a second document.
A decision about the release's own scope — no gate, no counter, no convergence effect. It asserts nothing about the world that could be false before the release exists.
